text:
This is the first Senators season since they traded their captain, Brady Tkachuk, to Florida in June, and the fallout is still loud: his father has taken shots at Ottawa fans over the exit. On the ice, the Senators have answered quietly. They're 11-6-2 with a 74% chance at the playoffs in our simulations, and they closed a five-game road trip with a 2-1 regulation win in Buffalo.

The record and the process agree. Ottawa gets 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and goals and expected goals are within a few of each other at both ends. Thomas Chabot and Jordan Spence have been the best pair, with 60% of the chances and a 12-6 goal edge.

What Ottawa hasn't found is a settled forward group. No line has played even an hour together at five on five, and the most used trio, Claude Giroux, Michael Amadio and Shane Pinto, is losing its minutes. The small sample with Tim Stutzle, Giroux and Fabian Zetterlund looks far better.

The week brought bad news too. Nick Cousins left Tuesday's overtime loss to Washington after a hit from Jakob Chychrun that drew no penalty, and Ottawa has had its own players in front of the league, with Hayden Hodgson suspended two games. In goal, Samuel Ersson has carried the load, and Jonas Johansson's demotion clears the way for Linus Ullmark's return. What to watch: who wins the net, and whether Stutzle gets the linemates to match.
headline: Life after Brady is going fine in Ottawa
